page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is a cost-optimized, Arm-based instance powered by the Ampere Altra processor family using Neoverse-N1 architecture. It provisioned with 16 shared 64-bit virtual CPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz, alongside 31.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, with no dedicated hardware GPU acceleration. Hypervisor operations are managed under QEMU.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. While Geekbench single-core performance (1052.0) falls into the weaker quartile and single-threaded bzip3 decompression ranks low at 7.08 GB/sec, multi-core benchmarks show sustained throughput. The stress-ng multi-core score reaches 29117.84, while the Geekbench multi-core score posts 8500.0. Clang software compilation benchmarks reflect solid compilation capability at 15304.0, while static web serving achieves 16.72 GB/sec and Redis SET operations deliver 22.71 million operations per second.

Because the 16 vCPUs operate on a shared allocation model, the instance prioritizes raw thread concurrency and cost-per-core density over guaranteed, dedicated CPU cycle reservations. Memory throughput remains balanced, delivering 102.2 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 57.91 GB/sec for write operations. However, AI inference tests reflect the limitations of the shared Arm cores lacking specialized matrix extensions, posting lower throughput on token generation.

The hardware configuration suits scale-out application tiers, multi-threaded CI/CD build environments, web serving, microservices, and general compute workloads where high core counts provide efficiency advantages over x86-based alternatives.
description: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm-based cloud instance powered by a 16-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz on a shared allocation schedule. It includes 31.0 GB of system memory and 320 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, with no GPU hardware present. Across synthetic benchmarks, the server balances modest single-core throughput (Geekbench single-core 1052.0) with consistent multi-core output (Geekbench multi-core 8500.0, stress-ng multi-core 29117.84). The platform achieves 16.72 GB/sec in static web throughput and 22.71 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, while memory bandwidth delivers 102.2 GB/sec for uncached large reads. With an approximately 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high core density, cax41 serves multi-threaded workloads, containerized web applications, microservices, and continuous integration pipelines prioritizing concurrent compute efficiency.
